questions.q: What does a capability evaluation measure?
options: Whether a model's behavior stays within acceptable bounds under adversarial conditions
What a model can do on a task when fully elicited, independent of whether it would do so in normal use
How quickly a model's weights can be fine-tuned
Whether a model's refusals survive jailbreak attempts
questions.explain: A capability evaluation asks whether a model can perform a task at its best, not whether it should or normally would.

questions.q: Why does 'full elicitation' matter when running a capability evaluation?
options: It doesn't matter — any prompting style gives the same score
Without deliberately drawing out the model's best performance, a capability score systematically underestimates what the model can actually do
Elicitation is only relevant for safety evaluations, not capability evaluations
Full elicitation guarantees the model will refuse harmful requests
questions.explain: A score taken from default, unprompted behavior understates true capability, which is why labs deliberately scaffold and prompt models to their best effort before scoring dangerous-capability evaluations.

questions.q: Which combination of capability and safety evaluation results represents the dangerous case this lesson highlights?
options: Weak capability and weak safety
Strong capability and strong safety
Strong capability and weak safety
Weak capability and strong safety
questions.explain: A model that is highly capable in a dangerous domain but whose behavioral safeguards don't reliably hold is the combination that matters most, since the capability is real and the safety measures aren't containing it.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the standard dangerous-capability categories described in this lesson?
options: Cyber-offense
Biological and chemical uplift
General coding proficiency
Autonomous replication and adaptation
questions.explain: General coding proficiency is an ordinary capability benchmark, not one of the dangerous-capability categories (cyber-offense, bio/chem uplift, autonomous replication, persuasion) where high capability itself is the risk.

questions.q: How do capability threshold results from evaluations like these actually get used, according to this lesson?
options: They are purely academic and have no bearing on real deployment decisions
They feed into governance structures such as Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy and OpenAI's Preparedness Framework, which require stronger safeguards once a threshold is crossed
They are used only to rank models on public leaderboards
They replace the need for any safety evaluation entirely
questions.explain: Capability evaluation results in these categories are tied directly to governance commitments that require additional safeguards or delay deployment once a defined threshold is crossed.
